item.title: Runtime problem with an application compiled with Crystal 1.21.1
item.author: MarioAriasC
item.content:encoded: The application compiles fine, but it fails when I try to run it.MBP 2026 with M5 processorCrystal installed through MacPortsWhen I compiled the application with I see this error.Unhandled exception: kevent: No such file or directory (RuntimeError) from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/errno.cr:48 in 'Crystal::EventLoop::Kqueue#initialize<Int32>:Nil' from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/gc/boehm.cr:193:7 in 'Thread#scheduler:Crystal::Scheduler' from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/crystal/scheduler.cr:31:5 in 'unbuffered_write' from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/crystal/once.cr:124:1 in 'main' from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/crystal/system/unix/main.cr:10:3 in 'main' If I compiled the application without , the error changes:Unhandled exception: Thread#execution_context cannot be nil (NilAssertionError) from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/crystal/event_loop.cr:35 in 'event_loop' from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/crystal/system/file_descriptor.cr:44:5 in 'unbuffered_write' from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/crystal/once.cr:124:1 in 'main' from /opt/local/share/crystal/src/crystal/system/unix/main.cr:10:3 in 'main' Same program compiled with previous versions ran fine.I suspect the MacPorts installation is broken.

item.title: CodeGraph support for Crystal — feedback wanted
item.author: n-rodriguez
item.content:encoded: It extracts modules, classes, structs, enums, lib/fun bindings, macros, accessor macros (getter/property…) and cross-file calls, inheritance and mixins. It indexes the compiler repo (2,423 files) as well as kemal and lavinmq.A/B on those three repos, 3 questions each, 2 runs per arm: wall-clock -46%, tool calls -65%, file reads -75%. Cost only -4%.macros are not expanded, so macro-generated methods (Kemal’s/ DSL) have no symbol;overloaded visitors () are where it falls back to grep: static extraction can’t tell which overload is reached.The PR has been waiting for review since July. If you work on Crystal code with an agent, trying the branch and reporting on the PR would help it land. Feedback on the extraction choices (macro expansion in particular) is welcome.I’m not affiliated with CodeGraph or its author in any way, beyond having submitted this PR as an outside contributor. Nothing to sell here: I just want to share what I’ve seen, because I think it can be useful to people writing Crystal with an agent.

item.title: Milestone: Running an Offline Kemal App with DNF on Fedora Linux! 🎉
item.author: renich
item.content:encoded:
We wanted to share an exciting milestone from our work on the ():Today, we successfully ran a Kemal web application inside a network-isolated container (), after installing Kemal directly as a system library with !No , no network calls, no , no , no local directory, and no vendored tarballs. Just:# dnf install crystal crystal-kemal And in a single script ():require "kemal"
get "/" do "Hello from Fedora Crystal (100% offline)!" end
Kemal.run Running immediately compiled, resolved all transitive dependencies (, , ), and served HTTP requests completely offline.While Fedora’s packaging guidelines permit standalone leaf applications to vendor dependencies (similar to Go and Rust using a ), distributing reusable shard libraries as unbundled system packages has historically been a challenge. Distributing compiled binaries doesn’t work for Crystal because of compile-time macros, generics monomorphization, and whole-program optimizations.We solved this through three simple mechanisms:: When building the Fedora compiler RPM, we injected /usr/share/crystal/shards into :CRYSTAL_PATH="lib:/usr/share/crystal/shards:/usr/share/crystal/src" : We package reusable shard libraries as uncompiled source trees into versioned directories (e.g. /usr/share/crystal/shards/kemal-1.14.0/). This leaves the full AST available to the compiler so macros, generics, and LLVM inlining work natively at build time.The LLVM Primary Symlink Model: To allow single scripts to do while still letting multiple library versions coexist on the system without RPM package collisions: The primary package provides an unversioned symlink:/usr/share/crystal/shards/kemal -> kemal-1.14.0Compatibility packages (like ) live in their own versioned directory without the unversioned symlink.For complex projects with a , our companion tool reads the lockfile and creates local symlinks in pointing directly to system packages—again, completely offline, reproducible, and without touching Git state.As a bonus during our verification, Crystal 1.21.1’s new concurrency model and multi-threaded fibers ran effortlessly in the same offline container. Resizing the default execution context or creating worker pools scaled smoothly across system threads:Observed threads: DEFAULT-0, DEFAULT-1, DEFAULT-2, DEFAULT-3 Concurrent compute fibers executed in parallel across all worker threads with zero hitches.What Does This Mean for the Ecosystem?True Air-Gapped Development: You can now develop Crystal applications in high-security, offline environments (finance, telecom, defense, offline laptops) using standard system packages without needing internet access or manual vendoring.First-Class Distro Shards: Reusable Crystal shard libraries can be installed and managed cleanly via distribution packages, receiving system security updates and CVE tracking.: Anyone can install a library with and immediately write a one-off script using without initializing a whole shard workspace.Come Join the Fedora Crystal SIG!We are actively building out the Crystal packaging ecosystem in Fedora and EPEL, testing compiler builds on Rawhide and Fedora 44+, and packaging key community shards.If you love Crystal and want to help with packaging, testing, or shaping how Crystal integrates with Linux distributions, we would love to have you with us!Cheers, & (AI pair programmer collaborating with Rénich)

item.title: Macro hook for full file
item.author: Jochen
item.content:encoded:
Ok, this one is probably going to be horrible, but hear me out. We are using Crystal a lot to create DSLs, and I wanted to put this out there and ask if other DSL authors would find this useful, too?One of the DSLs should have the following structure:require "horrible/dsl"
namespace Some::Namespace
# DSL Stuff goes here, all top level We now need to wrap everything following in some blocks (module, class, whatever). So we would need a hook that calls the namespace macro with everything below it as a block. I guess right now, there’s no way to do this.For added horribleness, there could be multiple namespaces, meaning each namespace macro would get as block the content up to the next namespace, or the end of the file.Sorry for inducing any pain, but them’s the requirements…

item.title: GitHub action for Ubuntu GETting 404 fetching dependencies
item.author: nogginly
item.content:encoded:
UPDATE: I have a workaround! See end of topic.Is anyone else seeing this? I tried searching the web but my isn’t strong apparently. - { os: ubuntu-latest, crystal: "1.20" } - { os: ubuntu-24.04-arm, crystal: latest } - { os: macos-latest, crystal: "1.21" } As of last night I started noticing that macOS runner is working but Linux ones are failing. The “annotation” on the actions says: Error: Command failed: sudo -n apt-get install -qy --no-install-recommends --no-upgrade -- libevent-dev libgmp-dev libpcre3-dev libssl-dev libxml2-dev libyaml-dev libpcre2-dev E: Failed to fetch http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/pool/main/libe/libevent/libevent-2.1-7t64_2.1.12-stable-9ubuntu2.1_arm64.deb 404 Not Found [IP: 91.189.91.102 80] E: Failed to fetch http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/pool/main/libe/libevent/libevent-extra-2.1-7t64_2.1.12-stable-9ubuntu2.1_arm64.deb 404 Not Found [IP: 91.189.91.102 80] E: Failed to fetch http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/pool/main/libe/libevent/libevent-openssl-2.1-7t64_2.1.12-stable-9ubuntu2.1_arm64.deb 404 Not Found [IP: 91.189.91.102 80] E: Failed to fetch http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/pool/main/libe/libevent/libevent-dev_2.1.12-stable-9ubuntu2.1_arm64.deb 404 Not Found [IP: 91.189.91.102 80] E: Unable to fetch some archives, maybe run apt-get update or try with --fix-missing? This CI workflow has worked as-is for weeks. If I should post this somewhere else, or if there is an active issue somewhere, please let me know. steps: - name: Force apt update (Linux only) if: ${{ runner.os == 'Linux' }} run: sudo -n apt-get update
- name: Checkout code uses: actions/checkout@v6
- name: Install Crystal uses: crystal-lang/install-crystal@v1 with: crystal: ${{matrix.crystal}} I added a Linux-specific forced before installing the Crystal install action and the workflows are succeeding again.
